newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's top oil refinery makes low sulphur diesel.
newsitem.headline: Russia's top oil refinery makes low sulphur diesel.

text.p: Russia's largest oil refinery, Omsk, has begun producing low sulphur diesel in line with new European quality standards, a company spokesman said on Monday.

Fillip Murashov, spokesman for Sibneft, the parent company of Omsk, said the refinery, located in Western Siberia, had unloaded its first 8,000 tonnes of diesel with a sulphur content of 0.05 percent, instead of the higher 0.20 percent.
"This is a first test run, and in time we will probably fully switch diesel production over to the low sulphur kind," he said, adding that the product was exported through the Baltics.
Omsk, southwest of Russia's cluster of refineries in the Urals, is many rail miles away from export markets and higher transport tariffs will be an issue.

Interfax news agency said Omsk might consider exporting higher sulphur diesel to European refineries for reprocessing through hydrotreaters, since domestic desulphurisation was adding $12-$14 per tonne to production costs.
The refinery, formally known as Omsknefteorgsintez, has an annual capacity of 566,300 barrels per day, but refined only 312,900 bpd in 1996, a 17 percent drop on 1995 levels.
Omsk, the only refining unit of vertically-integrated Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft), produced 5.24 million tonnes of diesel last year.
An October 1996 European Commission "green" directive requires all automotive gas oil (diesel) to have no more than 0.05 percent sulphur, below the earlier level of 0.20 percent.

Few Russian refineries are equipped to meet the new standards. The Kirishi refinery, near the port of St Petersburg, and the Norsi refinery, near Moscow, both make lower sulphur diesel. About five other Russian refineries have the technological capabilities to make cleaner material.
